channel.title: Brandon Leon
channel.description: Essays and research notes on public markets.

item.title: June Is When Micron Has to Do the Work
item.description: MU ran 38% in 17 trading days. June stops being about narrative and starts being about numbers. FQ3 prints June 24 — $33.5B revenue, 81% gross margin, $19.15 EPS. The cleanest test of the thesis we'll get. PT stays at $1,100; trim ladder continues.

item.title: Week Recap — May 25–29, 2026
item.description: Nine straight up weeks. Dell +33%, the best single day of its life. PCE came in at 3.3% Y/Y — hotter than every scenario we modeled. The eight-week mean-reversion call didn't survive Friday's tape. The pivot is rotation within the AI complex, not out of it.

item.title: I Bought Micron at $668. Here's Why I'm Not Buying at $881.
item.description: Three weeks ago the sell-side median sat around $549. On Tuesday UBS tripled their price target to $1,625 and Micron crossed $1 trillion. The variant view became consensus. The PT stays at $1,100 — now comes the harder discipline of trimming into strength.

item.title: Week Ahead — Week of May 26, 2026
item.description: NVIDIA crushed it, Walmart confirmed the consumer, the FOMC printed the most divided meeting since 1992. The S&P is 8-for-8 weeks. Friday's April PCE is the print that decides whether the Fed's hawkish minority had a point.

item.title: Week Ahead — Week of May 18, 2026
item.description: Three tests for the supercycle: the consumer (Home Depot, Walmart, TJX), the Fed (FOMC minutes — the most divided meeting since 1992), and NVIDIA after close. Wednesday May 20 is the binary that decides whether the seven-week ATH run extends or breaks.

item.title: Weekly Market Outlook — Week of May 11, 2026
item.description: The macro printed badly and the S&P printed higher. Hot CPI, soft retail, record-low Michigan sentiment, no Fed cuts — and a new all-time high anyway. The AI cycle is doing all the work. Recap plus what we're watching into next week's docket.

item.title: The Market Is Cooling Under the Semis
item.description: The market is not pumping because everything is fine. It is holding up because semiconductors, AI infrastructure, and quality earnings are offsetting a cooling economy. A market recap into Friday's payrolls, with macro data, an investment thesis, and four macro-level options ideas.

item.title: Weekly Market Outlook — Week of May 4, 2026
item.description: Soft-landing narrative meets sticky inflation, a concentrated AI rally, and an increasingly structural geopolitical tape. Ideas into payrolls, ISM Services, and JOLTS — plus four sector calls and four macro options structures.

item.title: The Fed After Powell
item.description: Notes on the April 29 FOMC meeting. The market is watching the rate path; the more differentiated story is the institution. Powell stays on the Board, four dissents, Warsh advances toward confirmation, and the under-priced risk shows up in term premium rather than the front-end policy path.
